newsitem.title: FINLAND: S&P UPGRADE NICE CHRISTMAS GIFT - FINNISH OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: S&P UPGRADE NICE CHRISTMAS GIFT - FINNISH OFFICIAL.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Tuesday upgrade of Finland's long-term foreign currency debt rating to AA from AA- was a recognition of Finland's economic policy, a senior official said on Tuesday.
"This was a nice Christmas gift," the finance ministry's finance director Kari Nars told Reuters.
"It is a tribute to the economic policy conducted."
The ministry said in a statement that it expected the upgrade to lower debt servicing expenses by 100 million to 130 million markka.
Nars said it was important that the U.S. credit rating agency said Finland appeared to be "one of the few countries that will easily meet the Maastricht deficit criteria".
"That was an important international recognition. It gives Finland a better seat to seek membership in EMU," he said.
He declined to comment on whether he expected Moody's Aa2 rating to be changed but noted that both institutes now have Finland at the third grade from the top.
Moody's issued its Aa2 rating for Finland in January 1992.
